title: External memory: history, profile and conversation state

videos.script: A support chat is not a list of questions. It is one customer, telling a story over twelve messages. {{alone}} Answer each message on its own, and one of Beatriz's five questions gets a right answer. Another gets an email address no document contains. {{history}} Send the whole conversation again every turn, and the prompt grows with every message. Twelve turns cost eight thousand tokens. The order number is found, and the replies start adding things of their own. {{rewrite}} The usual fix is to rewrite the question so it stands on its own. Here, every rewrite changed the question. Instead, the earlier turn most like the new one is put in front of it, for the search only. {{table}} Every turn goes into a table, with the account it belongs to. {{state}} And what the program knows for certain, the customer's name and order number, is written as a source. The model reads it, and still refuses to answer from it. That fact is the program's to say. {{accounts}} Leave the account out of one query, and Rafael's state carries Beatriz's order number. {{forget}} A memory of a customer is personal data. It needs an owner, a reason, and a way to be erased in one statement. {{end}}
